findings.summary: The explicit Fredricksen–Sweet coloring of {1,…,536}, its compact symmetric representation, and the exhaustive checker correctly verify all 71,824 admissible Schur triples, including x=y. The subject independently repeats the check and agrees entry-for-entry with the earlier supplied witness, strongly supporting S(6)≥536, though this bound is neither new nor original to the subject.

The blocker counts (64,43,55,38,32,35) follow from the supplied symmetric construction, sum to the 267 ordinary same-color symmetric pairs, and agree with the class sizes and exceptional pair {179,358}. Disjoint blocker pairs directly force at least 64 changes when C(537)=1 and at least 55 when C(537)=3, proving those two cases lie outside Hamming radius 43 without SAT certificates.

For fixed c=C(537), disjoint blocker pairs force b_c mandatory changes, while every remaining change is exactly either a second changed blocker endpoint or a change outside the blocker pairs. Hence d_H=b_c+#extras, yielding extra-change limits 0, 5, 11, and 8 for colors 2, 4, 5, and 6 respectively. Together with the direct exclusions for colors 1 and 3, this exhausts all labeled cases; the stated consequence under color permutations is also correct.

The generated CNF correctly enforces exactly one of six colors, all Schur constraints for the 72,092 triples through 537 including the x=y binary cases, the conditioned color of 537, the blocker-pair extra-change equivalences, and the appropriate Sinz at-most-k bound using signed literals. The recorded formula dimensions are internally consistent. The RUP-only LRAT checker design is sound: it validates ordered unit-propagation hints, derives clauses only after conflict, and accepts only after deriving the empty clause. No evident encoding or checker flaw invalidates the intended argument.

The universal radius-43 exclusion is not established by the supplied evidence. Colors 1 and 3 are proved directly, and the other four cases are correctly reduced to explicit finite CNFs, but the referenced compressed LRAT proofs for colors 2, 4, 5, and 6 are absent. Digests, proof statistics, expected output, regeneration instructions, and a verification request cannot replace replayable proof bytes. Supplying matching LRAT objects or independently regenerating and replaying them would resolve the gap.

Even if all four LRAT proofs are valid, the result is only a local exclusion within Hamming distance 43 of one fixed labeled baseline on the first 536 positions. It neither excludes distant or structurally unrelated colorings through 537 nor supplies a coloring of 537 or above. Therefore it implies neither S(6)=536 nor any improvement to 536≤S(6)≤1836.
